drivingQuestion: Against whose will were the Egyptian vessels lent — the Egyptians' or Israel's?
outcomeNote: Two anonymous versions stand side by side, each with its support; the sugya decides for neither.

segments.he: ״וַיַּשְׁאִלוּם״, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהִשְׁאִילוּם בְּעַל כָּרְחָם. אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי בְּעַל כָּרְחָם דְּמִצְרַיִם, וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי בְּעַל כָּרְחָם דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
segments.en: With regard to the spoils taken from Egypt described in the verse: “And the Lord gave the nation grace in the eyes of Egypt, «and they gave them what they requested» and they emptied Egypt” (Exodus 12:36), «Rabbi Ami said: This teaches that» the Egyptians «gave them what they requested against their will.» There is a dispute with regard to the question: Against whose will? «Some say» it was given «against the will of the Egyptians, and some say» it was given «against the will of Israel.» The proponent of each position cites support for his opinion.

segments.he: מַאן דְּאָמַר בְּעַל כָּרְחָם דְּמִצְרַיִם — דִּכְתִיב: ״וּנְוַת בַּיִת תְּחַלֵּק שָׁלָל״. מַאן דְּאָמַר בְּעַל כָּרְחָם דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל — מִשּׁוּם מַשּׂוֹי.
segments.en: «The one who said» that it was given «against the will of the Egyptians» cites the verse describing Israel’s exit from Egypt, «as it is written: “And she who tarries at home divides the spoils”» (Psalms 68:13). That which the woman in the verse requested from her counterpart was actually spoils taken against the will of an enemy. «The one who said» that it was given «against the will of Israel,» claims that they did not want the vessels «because of the» burden of carrying a heavy «load» on a long journey.

moves.summary: Lemma: Exodus 12:36, 'and they gave them what they requested'.
moves.about: the lemma 'and they gave them what they requested' (Exodus 12:36) opens the exposition

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אמי: מלמד שהשאילום בעל כרחם
moves.summary: R' Ami expounds: the verb teaches that the lending was under compulsion.
moves.about: the verb וישאלום teaches that the lending was done under compulsion

moves.summary: Second version (sibling of the first): the compulsion was on Israel.
moves.about: whose coercion R' Ami's 'against their will' refers to — the Egyptians' or Israel's

moves.cueHe: מאן דאמר בעל כרחם דמצרים — דכתיב
moves.summary: Support from Psalms 68:13: what was requested is called 'spoil', taken from an unwilling enemy.
moves.about: prooftext that what the women requested was 'spoil', i.e. taken against the enemy's will

moves.cueHe: מאן דאמר בעל כרחם דישראל — משום משוי
moves.summary: Support from reasoning: Israel did not want the burden of carrying a heavy load.
